extracted.intended_audience: copyholders, proofreaders, and editorial staff at publishers/presses
extracted.subtask_description: Practical rules and workplace practices for copyholders and proofreaders plus an index of detailed typographic and style rules for preparing manuscripts, proofs, and printed matter. Emphasizes proof-handling, signal systems, housekeeping, and many specific style/typography standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read proofs aloud with reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the proofs aloud so the reader hears you better and can watch your hand better; slow up the moment he puts his pencil to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the reader a chance to make corrections; pausing when the reader marks saves rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a private system of signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolve your own system of signals for marking (e.g., tap the table once for each word to be put in italics rather than saying 'in italics' repeatedly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals need only be intelligible to you and your reader; use voice-raising or tapping to indicate style treatments to save time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not waste time instructing on style
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not waste time over matters of style; the proofreader is supposed to know the rules without your telling him (for instance, which titles are set in italics vs. roman-quoted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume the proofreader/editor follows the established style rules; only query when rules do not resolve an issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be careful transferring marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful in transferring marks; a mark in the wrong place means two errors uncorrected in place of one corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate mark transfer prevents multiplication of errors; verify placement before finalizing corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure completeness and order when sending proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: In sending out proofs, see that everything is there; arrange the copy and proof-sheets neatly and consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check that all required materials accompany the proofs and that sheets are in correct sequence to avoid missing pages or mis-sends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult job ticket before first proof shipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Never send out proofs, for the first time, without consulting the job ticket for the number wanted, and the name and address of the person to whom they are to be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify quantity and recipient details to prevent logistical errors and incorrect shipments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply the correct manuscript with proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should accompany the galley-proof; the foul proof (author's marked galley-proof) should accompany the page-proof. If no galley-proof has been sent, the manuscript should accompany the page-proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include the appropriate manuscript/proof combo so recipients can reconcile marks and original text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label envelopes with contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate in the lower left-hand corner the contents of all the envelopes you address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear external labeling speeds mail handling and prevents misplacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fasten pins in a standard location
rubrics_metrics.description: Fasten your pins in the center at the top, not diagonally in the left-hand corner, thus covering up the directions, etc., often written there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent pin placement preserves important notations on sheets and keeps materials readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return reference volumes nightly
rubrics_metrics.description: Return every evening to the file or the bookcase any volume that may have been taken out for reference during the day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain shared reference availability and workplace order by nightly returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain tidy, well-organized proofroom records
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that you are the housekeeper of the proofroom; take pride in its neat and orderly appearance. Keeping the records, files, etc., naturally devolves upon you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perfect your system so everything can be located at a moment's notice; the more housekeeping you do unasked, and the better you do it, the more you will be appreciated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard proofreader's marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the conventional set of proofreader's marks for indicating corrections (e.g., Put in capitals; Put in SMALL CAPITALS; Put in LOWER CASE; Put in italics; Put in bold face; Dele (delete); turn letter; indent (make a new paragraph); put in space; close up—no space; bad spacing; wrong font; transpose; carry to the left/right; elevate; imperfect letter—correct; indicate space between words—shove down; straighten crooked line; restore words crossed out; print as a logotype; words omitted; query to author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put marks in capitals (or as specified) and use the conventional symbols consistently so compositors and authors can read and act on corrections reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles and works formatting (italics vs roman-quote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for which titles and divisions to set in italics and which to set in roman-quotation (books, essays, articles, pamphlets, newspapers, divisions of publications, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See detailed italics rules: italics for titles of books and other works (60); roman-quoted for some items such as divisions; exceptions and notes apply (e.g., lengthy bibliographical lists need not italicize).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive rules for capitalization covering proper nouns, titles, institutions, geographical names, historical epochs, governmental bodies, publications' titles, and many special categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules run from general principles (1-57) through many specific cases (academic degrees, names of bodies, titles, terms with acquired meanings). Consult the relevant section for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and their punctuation/spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on abbreviations: forms in literary references, no space between elements of some abbreviations, when to omit periods (e.g., initials used as abbreviations), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the rules for spacing and periods (see entries 52, 103, 123, 237).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation: comma, colon, dash, parentheses, ellipses, exclamation, interrogation
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed rules for use of commas (141-62), colons (131-36), dashes (166-75), parentheses (176-79), ellipses (180-81), exclamation points (127-28), and interrogation points (129-30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each punctuation mark has specific functions and exceptions (e.g., comma use with clauses, colon to introduce lists or statements, dash for emphasis or breaks). Consult sections for examples and boundary cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation and compound-word rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for hyphenated words, compounds, hyphenization, hyphens at line breaks, and the use of hyphens in forming compound adjectives and combinations (rules 182-214).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes lists of hyphenated words, how to indicate omitted common elements by hyphen, and guidance for negative particles, prefixes, and special combining forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of words (syllabification) and avoidance of divided words
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for dividing words at line endings, recommended systems of division, avoidance of unnecessary division, and special rules for foreign words (215-31).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dividing words at awkward places (e.g., next-to-last line), and follow the prescribed division system for the language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and numerals formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on when to spell out numbers vs use figures, treatment of consecutive numbers, commas in thousands, ordinals, and spacing for numerals in headlines and lines (94-100, 154, 159, 173, 271).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat numbers consistently in connected groups; small numbers spelled out in running text, large/technical groups in figures; consult specific rules for dates, centuries, and ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics usage details
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for italics including emphasis, foreign words, names of genera/species, initial words in resolutions, titles, and when italics need not be used in long bibliographies (58-73).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use italics for emphasis and certain names/terms, but avoid overuse; refer to section numbers for fine distinctions and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations and citations formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for quoting passages, reduction of citations, punctuation of quotations, use of ibid./op. cit./loc. cit., and formatting literary references (74-87, 233, 237).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules govern brief quotations vs longer quoted passages, placement of punctuation, and reference shorthand in footnotes and bibliographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes and indexing conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for footnotes (numbering, placement of index figures, general style 232-39), use of daggers/asterisks for indexes, and indexing rules including alphabetizing and treatment of particles and prefixes (232-40).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow machine-specific and house rules for footnote sequence, indices, and cross-references; use standard symbols for different note levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables, figures, and illustrations rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for setting tables (open tables, headlines, columns of figures) and for letters referring to parts of illustrations/figures (241-50, 68).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use leaders for blanks, double rules, appropriate spacing, and distinct type for averages/generalizations where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing, leading, and typographic measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing even spacing, hair-spaces, em/en spaces, leading ('leaded'), spacing of formulas and figures, spacing after abbreviations, and general spacing conventions (259-77, 269-73).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid hair-spacing, ensure even spacing throughout, and apply machine-specific spacing rules for linotype/monotype as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fonts, types, and correct font selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on typefaces (face, font, bold-face, brevier, minion, nonpareil, long primer), wrong font identification, and how to indicate type changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate font changes using the prescribed proofreader's marks and follow house standards for type naming and sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings, headlines, and paragraph/indention rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and setting instructions for headings, center-heads, cut-in-heads, box-heads, headlines, paragraph styles, indention rules and hanging indention (279-84, 274-76).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prescribed capitalization and omission-of-period rules for headlines and use specific indentation styles for quoted matter and paragraphing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names, alphabetizing, and indexing of personal/place names
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for alphabetizing names, treatment of particles in foreign names ('van', 'de', 'O' variants), indexing of umlauts, and capitalization/indexing exceptions (240, 3, 240 notes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistent indexing rules for family/particle forms and special characters; consult the indexing section for machine-specific treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special subdivisions and lists punctuation/format
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions for enumerations, use of parentheses for subdivisions, placement of punctuation in lists, and the format of serialized divisions (176, 176-79).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parentheses/letters/numbers for subdivisions and follow rules for punctuation within enumerations and nested parentheses/brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign words and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for foreign words and phrases: retention of accents, italicizing foreign words incorporated into English, quotation of English equivalents, and division of foreign-language words (59, 78, 231).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italicize foreign words generally; retain accents where appropriate; supply English equivalents when required and follow division rules for the language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-specific typesetting notes (linotype/monotype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on spacing and footnote numbering differences for Linotype and Monotype machines, their explained parts and use, and suggested practices for matter set on these machines (293-94, 259-60, 239).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of different machine conventions (spacing, footnote numbering, leaders) and apply the house rules appropriate to the compositor's machine.
